title: The fibres of an etale morphism are disjoint unions of spectra of finite separable field extensions
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], let $s\in S$ with residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Then $X_s$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(s)$: the underlying topological space of $X_s$ is discrete (every point of $X_s$ is open and closed in $X_s$), and for every point $y\in X_s$ the open subscheme $\{y\}$ [def-pc-scheme] of $X_s$ is isomorphic over $\kappa(s)$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], where the residue field $\kappa(y)$ is a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of $\kappa(s)$ every element of which is a root of a separable polynomial over $\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-separable-polynomial].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02GL (morphisms-lemma-etale-over-field, label at line 8175), part (2) (line 8186); Stacks writes out only the proof of part (1) (lines 8191-8207: via Algebra, Lemma 00U3 = algebra-lemma-etale-over-field, algebra.tex line 39394, and Morphisms, Lemma 01TE = morphisms-lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre, line 3565); part (2) is part (1) applied to X_s -> Spec kappa(s), etale by Morphisms, Lemma 02GO (morphisms-lemma-base-change-etale, line 8136)

proof.text: The fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is a scheme over $\kappa(s)$ through the second projection $p:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, which is the base change of the etale morphism $f:X\to S$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$. By clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (with $V=S$, $W=X\xrightarrow{f}S$, $U=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$) the projection $p$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02GO (morphisms-lemma-base-change-etale, line 8136), which reduces part (2) of Lemma 02GL to part (1)

proof.text: Let $y\in X_s$. Since $X_s$ is a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $y$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X_s$ and an isomorphism $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ for a commutative ring $C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}C\cong U\hookrightarrow X_s\xrightarrow{p}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is etale: the inclusion of the open subscheme $U$ is an open immersion, hence etale, and a composite of etale morphisms is etale (clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; an isomorphism is an open immersion), with step 1. Every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a unique ring map $\kappa(s)\to C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; this makes $C$ a $\kappa(s)$-algebra with $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] there are $n\ge0$, fields $L_1,\dots,L_n$, each a finite and separable algebraic extension of $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and a $\kappa(s)$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:C\xrightarrow{\sim}L_1\times\cdots\times L_n$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02GL, proof, lines 8201-8203 ("for any affine open U of X we see that U is a finite disjoint union of spectra of finite separable field extensions of k"), using Algebra, Lemma 00U3

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields] to $L_1\times\cdots\times L_n$ with projections $\pi_j$, and transport along the isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}(L_1\times\cdots\times L_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}C\cong U$. The point $y\in U$ corresponds to $\mathfrak p_j=\ker\pi_j$ for exactly one $j$ (clause 1); the set $\{y\}$ is open in $U$ (clause 2), hence open in $X_s$ since $U$ is open in $X_s$; and the morphism $\iota_y:\operatorname{Spec}L_j\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}\pi_j}\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_iL_i)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}\alpha}\operatorname{Spec}C\cong U\hookrightarrow X_s$ is an open immersion (clause 3, composed with an isomorphism and the inclusion of an open subscheme) with image $\{y\}$, i.e. it is an isomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}L_j$ onto the open subscheme $\{y\}$ of $X_s$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Since $\pi_j\circ\alpha$ is a homomorphism of $\kappa(s)$-algebras, functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $p\circ\iota_y=\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(s)\to L_j)$: the isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}L_j\cong\{y\}$ is an isomorphism over $\kappa(s)$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02GL, proof, lines 8201-8207 ("U is a finite disjoint union of spectra ...; thus X is a discrete space"); the finite disjoint union is Algebra, Lemma 00ED applied n-1 times

proof.text: By step 3 every point of $X_s$ is open, so every subset of $X_s$, being the union of its points, is open: the space $X_s$ is discrete; in particular every point is also closed (its complement is a union of open points). (Stacks first shows that all points are closed, by Morphisms, Lemma 01TE, since their residue fields are algebraic over $\kappa(s)$, and concludes discreteness from the finite discrete affine opens; the openness of the points from step 3 gives both at once, so Lemma 01TE is not needed.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02GL, proof, lines 8203-8207 (all points closed via Lemma 01TE; "Thus X is a discrete space")

proof.text: The residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is the residue field at $y$ of the open subscheme $\{y\}$ (the stalk of $\mathcal O_{X_s}$ at $y$ equals that of the open subscheme containing $y$ [def-pc-scheme]). Through the isomorphism $\iota_y$ over $\kappa(s)$ of step 3 it is identified, compatibly with the maps from $\kappa(s)$, with the residue field of $\operatorname{Spec}L_j$ at its single point, which is $L_j$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Hence $\kappa(y)\cong L_j$ as extensions of $\kappa(s)$, so $\kappa(y)/\kappa(s)$ is finite and separable algebraic (step 2) [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]: every element of $\kappa(y)$ is a root of its minimal polynomial over $\kappa(s)$, which is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial]. Finally $\{y\}\cong\operatorname{Spec}L_j\cong\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ over $\kappa(s)$, the second isomorphism being $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the $\kappa(s)$-isomorphism $\kappa(y)\cong L_j$. With step 4 this is the statement.
